title: Dialysis using D-Tubes
author: Neilier Junior
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bhqkj5uw

steps.title: Select dialysis cut‑off
steps.instruction: Choose a D‑Tube cut‑off membrane between 3.5 kDa and 14 kDa appropriate for the biomolecule to be purified.

steps.title: Equilibrate tube with water
steps.instruction: Fill the selected D‑Tube with Milli‑Q water, let it equilibrate for 15 minutes, then discard the water.

steps.title: Weigh empty tube
steps.instruction: Weigh the equilibrated dialysis tube and record its mass.

steps.title: Load sample
steps.instruction: Using a pipette, add the sample to the tube, then weigh the tube again and record the new mass.

steps.title: Prepare dialysis bath
steps.instruction: Fill a beaker with 1000 mL of Milli‑Q water (or the desired exchange buffer) and place a magnetic stir bar inside.

steps.title: Immerse dialysis tube
steps.instruction: Place the dialysis tube on a floating rack and submerge it in the beaker containing the 1000 mL bath.

steps.title: Dialysis with conductivity monitoring
steps.instruction: Cover the beaker with plastic film, start magnetic stirring, and monitor the conductivity of the bath solution. Continue until conductivity no longer rises, indicating equilibrium between sample and bath.

substeps.instruction: If conductivity cannot be monitored, dialyze for 1 hour; this duration is sufficient to desalt 3 M ammonium sulfate under the described conditions.

steps.title: Recover and weigh sample
steps.instruction: Remove the dialysis tube from the beaker, open it, and weigh the recovered sample contents.
